note: Client construction, the options class, DI registration and server/base-URL selection.

assertions.claim: An APIMatic .NET SDK exposes exactly one public client class, and it is sealed.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client — 'one public client class'; dotnet-testing § the seam (you fake the HttpClient, not the client)

assertions.claim: public {Api}Client(HttpClient httpClient, {Api}ClientOptions options) — the HttpClient comes first and the options type is the client type name plus 'Options'. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client, the constructor code block; dotnet-testing § the seam

assertions.claim: That constructor is the client's ONLY public constructor — there is no parameterless or options-only overload, so an HttpClient must always be supplied.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client; dotnet-testing § the seam

assertions.claim: The SDK does not own the HttpClient — the client implements no IDisposable and disposes nothing, so it neither needs nor accepts a using block.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § HttpClient lifetime — 'The SDK does not own the HttpClient — you provide it.'

assertions.claim: Nothing anywhere in the SDK disposes the HttpClient it was handed — its lifetime is entirely the caller's, which is what makes one long-lived instance (or IHttpClientFactory) safe.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § HttpClient lifetime

assertions.claim: Each API group is a get-only property on the client named after its controller type, so a grouped operation is called client.{ApiGroup}.{Operation}(...). Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client — 'grouped under controller properties ... called client.{ApiGroup}.{Operation}(...)'

assertions.claim: An operation that belongs to no group sits directly on the client and obeys the same signature template as a grouped one — requestOptions second-to-last, ct last.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client — 'an operation that belongs to no group sits directly on the client'; dotnet-calling-endpoints § signature template

assertions.claim: The client reads options.Environment once, in its constructor, and hands the ServerOptions object itself to the Server — which is why assigning options.Environment after construction silently does nothing. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § ServerOptions configuration for each Environment — 'Environment and Server are not read at the same time'

assertions.claim: The generated client sends X-APIMatic-Gen-Version: 4.0.0. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: the core-surface stamp at the top of every dotnet-* skill

assertions.claim: The resilience pipelines are built in the client constructor from options.Retry — so retry configuration is a per-client choice fixed at construction, not a per-call one. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § HttpClient lifetime — 'two Polly pipelines are eagerly built from options.Retry'; dotnet-configuration-resilience § Retries

assertions.claim: The options class is a plain public class named {Api}ClientOptions — not a record, no base type — so the object-initializer form the samples use compiles. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client, the options code block

assertions.claim: The options class always carries these four knobs, get/set, in this order — Environment = ServerEnvironment.Default(), Retry = RetryOptions.Default(), Logging = new(), Server = new(). Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client — 'The options class always carries these knobs'; the 'This surface HAS: LoggingOptions on the options class' stamp

assertions.claim: No member of the options class is `required`, so new {Api}ClientOptions() compiles — auth is not needed for a stub.
assertions.defends: dotnet-testing § A reusable stub handler — 'new {Api}ClientOptions { /* auth not needed for stubs */ }'

assertions.claim: Every property beyond the four fixed knobs — the per-scheme credentials and the OAuth2 token-strategy hook — is nullable and carries no initializer; nothing on the options class has to be set for it to construct.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § the options code block — 'one nullable credentials property per auth scheme'; dotnet-authentication § how APIMatic surfaces each scheme

assertions.claim: For an OAuth2 scheme the options class exposes a {OAuthProperty}TokenStrategy immediately alongside the credentials, typed over that same credentials type.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § the options code block — 'a nullable {Scheme}TokenStrategy hook alongside it'; dotnet-authentication § Supplying your own token source

assertions.claim: ServerEnvironment lives in {RootNamespace}.Servers and is a StringEnum record, not a C# enum — which is why every construction sample carries `using {RootNamespace}.Servers;`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Direct instantiation (the using list) and § Choosing the server / base URL

assertions.claim: ServerEnvironment exposes a static Default() method returning the API's default environment — the value options.Environment is initialised to and every sample assigns.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Direct instantiation — 'Environment = ServerEnvironment.Default()'

assertions.claim: options.Server is a ServerOptions holding nothing but one {ServerName}Options property per server the API defines, each named after its own type and defaulted — there is nothing settable directly on ServerOptions.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § ServerOptions configuration for each Environment — 'It exposes one {ServerName}Options per server the API defines'; dotnet-client-initialization § Choosing the server / base URL — 'NOT directly on ServerOptions'

assertions.claim: Server options are nested per server AND per environment: {ServerName}Options carries one {Environment}Options property named after the environment, and that nested class carries the BaseUrl — always present and settable. The override path is options.Server.{ServerName}.{Environment}.BaseUrl. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § ServerOptions configuration for each Environment; dotnet-client-initialization § Choosing the server / base URL

assertions.claim: The environment you select is what picks the BaseUrl the request URL is built from — only that environment's options are read. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § ServerOptions configuration for each Environment — 'only that environment's options are read'

assertions.claim: The client keeps a live reference to the ServerOptions object and re-resolves the URL through it on every request — so editing options.Server.{ServerName}.{Environment}.BaseUrl after construction does take effect, unlike reassigning options.Environment.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § ServerOptions configuration for each Environment — 'keeps a live reference to the ServerOptions object and re-resolves the URL on every request'

assertions.claim: The DI extension class sits in the SDK's root namespace, so `using {RootNamespace};` is all a Program.cs needs for Add{Api}Client to bind.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Dependency injection, the snippet's `using {RootNamespace};`

assertions.claim: Every APIMatic .NET SDK ships an IServiceCollection extension named Add{Api}Client — the client type name prefixed with 'Add' — taking an optional Action<{Api}ClientOptions> and returning IServiceCollection, so both services.Add{Api}Client(); and the configure-callback form compile and chain.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Dependency injection — 'Every APIMatic .NET SDK ships a ServiceCollection extension named Add{Api}Client'

assertions.claim: There is exactly one registration overload, and its callback is handed only the options object — never an IServiceProvider — so the callback cannot read container services, scoped or otherwise.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Dependency injection — 'the callback may read IConfiguration or environment variables, but not scoped services'

assertions.claim: The configure callback is invoked once, at registration — outside and before the singleton factory — and the options object it mutates is the one captured for the client's whole life.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Dependency injection — 'captures the options you configure once, at registration'

assertions.claim: Add{Api}Client itself calls AddHttpClient() with no name — which registers an ILoggerFactory, so on the DI path logging is already on and the {APICLIENTTYPENAME}_LOG environment variable never fires.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging — 'Add{Api}Client always fills it (it calls AddHttpClient(), which registers an ILoggerFactory)'

assertions.claim: The singleton factory returns the concrete {Api}Client, so the registered service type is the client class itself — GetRequiredService<{Api}Client>() resolves it and there is no SDK interface to register against.
assertions.defends: dotnet-testing § DI-based construction — 'services.BuildServiceProvider().GetRequiredService<{Api}Client>()'; dotnet-client-initialization § Dependency injection (the constructor-injection snippet)

assertions.claim: Controller types are constructed only by the client — their constructors are internal, so the one public client class is the only entry point to an operation.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § Shape of the client — 'one public client class'
